# netapp-ontap_fpolicy_policy (Resource)

Creates, updates, and deletes an FPolicy policy resource.

### Related ONTAP commands
```
vserver fpolicy policy create
vserver fpolicy policy modify
vserver fpolicy policy delete
vserver fpolicy policy show
```

### Supported Platforms
* On-prem ONTAP system 9.6 or higher
* Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "netapp-ontap_fpolicy_policy" "example" {
  cx_profile_name  = "cluster4"
  svm_name         = "carchi-test"
  name             = "compliance-monitoring-policy"
  engine           = "compliance_engine"
  events           = ["file_access_event", "nfs_compliance_event"]
  priority         = 1
  mandatory        = false
  passthrough_read = false
  
  scope = {
    include_volumes = ["vol1", "vol2"]
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:

### Required

- `cx_profile_name` - (String) Connection profile name.
- `name` - (String) Specifies the name of the FPolicy policy. This field cannot be changed after creation.
- `svm_name` - (String) Name of the SVM to which this FPolicy policy belongs. This field cannot be changed after creation.
- `events` - (Set of String) List of event names that will be used for event monitoring.
- `priority` - (Number) Priority for this FPolicy policy. The value must be between 1 and 10. The lower the number, the higher the priority.
- `scope` - (Block) Scope of the policy. Applies to the FPolicy policy to specific volumes, shares, export policies, or file extensions (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--scope)).

### Optional

- `engine` - (String) Name of the engine to use with this policy.
- `mandatory` - (Bool) Specifies whether file access is blocked if the policy engine is unavailable. If set to true, file access events will be blocked when the policy engine is unavailable.
- `passthrough_read` - (Bool) Specifies whether passthrough-read should be allowed for FPolicy servers registered for the policy.
- `privileged_user` - (String) Specifies the privileged user name.
- `allow_privileged_access` - (Bool) Specifies whether privileged access is allowed. This field can only be set during updates, not during creation.

### Read-Only

- `id` - (String) FPolicy policy identifier in the format `svm_name/policy_name`.

<a id="nestedblock--scope"></a>

### Nested Schema for `scope`

Optional:

- `include_volumes` - (Set of String) List of volumes to include in the FPolicy policy scope.
- `exclude_volumes` - (Set of String) List of volumes to exclude from the FPolicy policy scope.
- `include_extension` - (Set of String) List of file extensions to include in the FPolicy policy scope.
- `exclude_extension` - (Set of String) List of file extensions to exclude from the FPolicy policy scope.
- `include_shares` - (Set of String) List of shares to include in the FPolicy policy scope.
- `exclude_shares` - (Set of String) List of shares to exclude from the FPolicy policy scope.
- `include_export_policies` - (Set of String) List of export policies to include in the FPolicy policy scope.
- `exclude_export_policies` - (Set of String) List of export policies to exclude from the FPolicy policy scope.
- `check_extensions_on_directories` - (Bool) Specifies whether the file extension check also applies to directory objects.
- `object_monitoring_with_no_extension` - (Bool) Specifies whether to monitor files that have no extension.

## Import

This resource supports import, which allows you to import existing FPolicy policies into the state.
Import require a unique ID composed of the policy name, SVM name, and the connection profile, separated by a comma.

id = `name`,`svm_name`,`cx_profile_name`

### Terraform Import

For example

```shell
terraform import netapp-ontap_fpolicy_policy.example compliance-monitoring-policy,carchi-test,cluster4
```

!> The terraform import CLI command can only import resources into the state. Importing via the CLI does not generate configuration. If you want to generate the accompanying configuration for imported resources, use the import block instead.

### Terraform Import Block

This requires Terraform 1.5 or higher, and will auto create the configuration for you

First create the block

```terraform
import {
  to = netapp-ontap_fpolicy_policy.fpolicy_import
  id = "compliance-monitoring-policy,carchi-test,cluster4"
}
```

Next run, this will auto create the configuration for you

```shell
terraform plan -generate-config-out=generated.tf
```

This will generate a file called generated.tf, which will contain the configuration for the imported resource

```terraform
# __generated__ by Terraform
# Please review these resources and move them into your main configuration files.

# __generated__ by Terraform from "compliance-monitoring-policy,carchi-test,cluster4"
resource "netapp-ontap_fpolicy_policy" "fpolicy_import" {
  cx_profile_name  = "cluster4"
  name             = "compliance-monitoring-policy"
  svm_name         = "carchi-test"
  engine           = "compliance_engine"
  events           = ["file_access_event", "nfs_compliance_event"]
  priority         = 1
  mandatory        = true
  passthrough_read = false
  
  scope = {
    include_volumes = ["vol1"]
  }
}
```
